# SILICON COVERAGE POLICY — one axis per line (paiml/infra#361).
#
#   <axis-id>  <status>  <runs-on labels, comma-separated>  # note
#
# STATUS is one of:
#   required        this axis MUST have a runner that can serve its selector.
#                   If none exists, silicon-nightly FAILS — a lane that silently
#                   stops covering an architecture is indistinguishable from one
#                   that never covered it.
#   pending:<issue> the axis is declared but not yet runnable. It does NOT fail
#                   the lane — AND IT CANNOT ROT: the preflight fails if a runner
#                   able to serve the selector APPEARS, because at that point the
#                   only thing standing between us and the coverage is this line.
#
# WHY A POLICY FILE AND NOT A MATRIX. aprender's correctness is silicon-dependent
# — SIMD paths, CUDA kernels, arch intrinsics, float behaviour — and the axes we
# do NOT cover are the interesting number. A `matrix:` lists what runs; this
# lists what SHOULD run and makes the gap a value rather than an absence.
#
# The gap was widened deliberately once: paiml/aprender#2740 made cuda-nightly
# gx10-only because its x86_64 GPU leg ran on lambda-labs, which must never be a
# CI host (paiml/infra#359). sm_89 was the STABLE reference and sm_121 the
# higher-risk target with a history of JIT bugs, so we gated only the risky one.
# That hole is CLOSED as of 2026-09-13 -- see the promotion note below -- and
# the remaining gap is one axis, aarch64-cuda-sm87.

x86_64-cpu          required        self-hosted,clean-room,intel
aarch64-cuda-sm121  required        self-hosted,gpu,gx10,cuda,blackwell

# ── promoted 2026-09-13: the runners appeared, so the hole closed ───────────
# The policy's own rule is that a pending axis CANNOT ROT: when a runner able
# to serve the selector shows up, the only thing between us and the coverage is
# the line. Both of these tripped that rule on the same day.
#
#   x86_64-cuda-sm89  yoga-gpu (self-hosted,Linux,X64,gpu,cuda,yoga,ada).
#                     The hole existed because the x86_64 GPU leg used to run on
#                     lambda-labs, which must never be a CI host (infra#359).
#                     yoga-gpu is a proper self-hosted Ada card, so the reason is
#                     gone. ci.yml's `cuda-unit` does touch yoga, but only on a
#                     pull_request AND only when gpu_touched==1 -- conditional
#                     coverage is not an axis, which is why this lane now runs it.
#   aarch64-macos     mini-m4 (self-hosted,ARM64,macOS,apple-silicon,m4,mini).
#                     The only darwin/arm64 silicon the repo has.
#
# Each has a job below; `required` here and no job there would claim coverage
# this lane does not produce.
x86_64-cuda-sm89    required        self-hosted,gpu,yoga,cuda,ada
aarch64-macos       required        self-hosted,mini,macos,arm64

# ── declared, not yet runnable ──────────────────────────────────────────────
aarch64-cuda-sm87   pending:361     self-hosted,gpu,jetson,cuda,orin
